lessons: Keep first-person narratives concise and ensure the central supernatural encounter happens early to sustain viewer retention.
Classic radio-drama formats with distinct atmospheric elements perform better when split into tighter, high-tension episodes.
Urban legends and specific regional settings (such as Kolkata locations) generate higher initial click-through interest than generic village settings.
Maintain a steady narrative pace in the middle chapters where viewer drop-off tends to spike, keeping dialogues sharp and grounded.
End episodes on sharp narrative cliffhangers involving moral dilemmas or imminent threats to drive engagement and comments.
titles: Titles featuring specific, eerie imagery (e.g., blood, number of a room/train, specific local objects) outperform generic horror titles.
First-person perspectives framed as lived experiences ('that happened to me') create immediate curiosity and higher click-through intent.
Using localized Bengali place names combined with an uncanny event (like 'Tollygunge last metro' or specific district houses) captures local audience interest best.
requests: Stories involving hidden ghosts or visual easter eggs where viewers count how many times the ghost appears
Local folklore and ghost stories specific to the viewers' own districts and towns via the map link
Continuation and resolution of mystery-driven character arcs (like Anirban's diary or Bhairab Thakur's cases)
Interactive moral choices and questions posed to the audience regarding the characters' decisions
